headline: OCTA Poll: Neighborhood Safety Perception Falls to 72% Nationwide
seoTitle: OCTA: Neighborhood Safety Perception Falls to 72% | FMB News
seoDescription: An OCTA survey found 72% of Filipinos feel safe in their neighborhoods, down from 87% in March 2023, with Metro Manila falling to 58%.
deck: Metro Manila recorded the sharpest decline, with neighborhood safety confidence falling from 91% to 58% in the latest OCTA survey.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Seventy-two percent of adult Filipinos said they feel safe in their neighborhoods in the latest OCTA Research Tugon ng Masa survey, down from 87% in March 2023.
The decline was steepest in Metro Manila, where the share saying they feel safe fell from 91% to 58%. Agreement that it is safe to walk alone at night in the capital fell from 88% to 48%.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The survey was conducted from July 4 to 11 among 1,200 adults and carries a national margin of error of plus or minus three percentage points.

OCTA cautioned that perceptions of safety can be influenced not only by crime levels but also by news and social-media exposure. The findings therefore measure public sentiment, not a direct count of crimes.

sections.heading: PNP trust
paragraphs: A separate OCTA result reported by The Philippine Star found 65% of respondents trusted the Philippine National Police and 63% were satisfied with its performance. That corrects the approved email brief's lower 60% trust figure.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: A fall in perceived safety can affect commuting behavior, neighborhood activity, school and business confidence, and public expectations of police visibility even when changes in actual crime incidence differ from changes in sentiment.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Future OCTA rounds and official crime statistics will show whether the decline in confidence persists and whether public perceptions move in the same direction as reported crime trends.
